transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Evan M., Priya N., Jordan E., Talia R., Mark Z.

Summary (auto): Align on legal redlines, security docs, and commercial pilot.

00:00 Speaker 1 - Evan: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Uh this is Evan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
00:08 Speaker 2 - Jordan: Good thanks, hey Evan. We're excited to get this moving — procurement wanted a short sync to cover the MSA and DPA points plus some basics on SLAs and encryption.
00:18 Speaker 3 - Talia: Hi, Talia here. From InfoSec I mostly care about key management, audit logs, and whether we can get a vendor hosted KMS or use our own HSM.
00:27 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yeah, hi everyone. I'll try to cover the technical bits, including private deployment options, our Dedicated tier, and the VPC peering model.
00:35 Speaker 1 - Evan: Cool. Agenda for us: quick MSA/DPA callouts, SLA/latency expectations, KMS/SSO, then next steps.

02:12 Speaker 2 - Jordan: So first on MSA, legal is mostly concerned about data processing clauses in the DPA — retention, subprocessors, and audit rights. Any quick color on Redwood's stance?
02:28 Speaker 4 - Priya: On subprocessors we maintain a list and we can add Aperture to the notification path; for hosted inference we do use cloud GPUs in partner regions, but for Dedicated or Private you get more control. Note: sometimes the transcript shows "Redwood dedicate" in the notes, but it's Dedicated tier.
02:46 Speaker 3 - Talia: Right, we want to avoid any third-party copying of PHI. Aperture handles health data, so the DPA needs to allow us to control retention and deletion — and show proof of deletion on termination.
03:05 Speaker 1 - Evan: Understood. Our standard DPA has data retention controls and deletion with certificate proof; we can attach an addendum for stricter retention for regulated data. I'll mark that as an action.

05:10 Speaker 4 - Priya: On the infra side, two options typically: Hosted API (fast onboarding) or Redwood Dedicated, which gives you a private GPU pool with network isolation. Dedicated supports customer-managed VPC peering and can be configured to use customer KMS via HSM integrations — though the on-prem package is a different path if you need air-gap.
05:35 Speaker 3 - Talia: If we use customer KMS, who holds the keys for runtime decryption of KV cache? We need to ensure keys never leave our HSM.
05:48 Speaker 4 - Priya: Good question. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS and have a key wrap pattern so the raw keys stay in your HSM. There is an operational handshake though, we'll need your cloud team to open specific lanes.
06:12 Speaker 5 - Mark: Slightly technical, but what's the expected p99 latency on Dedicated for 1k token responses? We need to ensure low-latency for patient-facing features.
06:26 Speaker 4 - Priya: Based on similar customers, with Dedicated and optimized kernels you're looking at 200–400ms per token on our T4-like pools, but that varies with model and sequence length. We'll share precise benchmark artifacts.
06:40 Speaker 1 - Evan: Also, pricing. Procurement flagged egress and KMS costs as unknowns. We normally itemize network egress and any KMS call charges — happy to put together a model.

08:55 Speaker 2 - Jordan: On SLAs — procurement wants 99.9% uptime for the Dedicated pool and remedies for prolonged outages. What's Redwood's typical SLA?
09:08 Speaker 1 - Evan: Our Dedicated SLA is 99.95% for the reserved pool, with crediting tiers. For hosted, we have a different SLA. We can include canary fallback policies in the MSA so customer traffic fails over to a compatible hosted model during a region outage, subject to data handling terms.
09:27 Speaker 3 - Talia: Fallback is okay only if data residency agreements are honored. If data must stay in EU region, we can't fail over to a US region without further controls.
09:39 Speaker 4 - Priya: We can set region pinning in routing policies. The smart routing can route by region and customer tier so you don't cross residency boundaries.

11:50 Speaker 5 - Mark: Procurement will want a cost example: committed capacity price vs burst credits. Also, is there a minimum commit?
12:03 Speaker 1 - Evan: Typical reserves start at a monthly minimum — we can do short pilots with a pilot discount. I'll send the pricing matrix. For charges: base reserved cost, per-token tier for overages, and potential egress/KMS pass-through.
12:18 Speaker 2 - Jordan: If we do a pilot, how long and what acceptance criteria?
12:25 Speaker 4 - Priya: A two-week dedicated pilot to validate latency and throughput is common. Acceptance criteria: p95 and p99 latency targets, error rate below 0.5%, and sample output quality checks run by your product team.

14:40 Speaker 3 - Talia: On security paperwork, we need SOC2 Type II report and vulnerability scanning cadence. Do you have SOC2?
14:50 Speaker 1 - Evan: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II attested — we'll share the report under NDA. We also offer penetration test results on request and continuous scanning.
15:02 Speaker 3 - Talia: Also need an audit log feed and retention of API logs for 90 days.
15:10 Speaker 4 - Priya: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3 shipper, retention configurable. Note there may be cost implications for long-term storage.

17:22 Speaker 2 - Jordan: A couple of specific MSA redline asks: limitation of liability amounts, indemnity carveouts for regulatory fines, and a data breach notification timeframe. We usually push for 30 days for notification, is that acceptable?
17:37 Speaker 1 - Evan: We can do 30 days for initial notification and then follow-up remediation plans; liability caps are negotiable depending on enterprise terms and commitment. We'll flag the liability clause for legal review.

19:55 Speaker 5 - Mark: What about subnet peering and egress IPs — we need a stable set for firewall allowlisting.
20:06 Speaker 4 - Priya: For Dedicated we provide a consistent egress range and can coordinate to give the list. For hosted, ranges are broader and depend on region. We'll produce the allowlist doc.

22:45 Speaker 3 - Talia: Encryption-at-rest: can we ensure customer data at rest is encrypted with our key?
22:53 Speaker 4 - Priya: Yes for Dedicated, you can use customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can explore a KMS integration. We'll note the exact encryption flows in the security appendix.

25:12 Speaker 2 - Jordan: Are there any export controls or data residency constraints we should be aware of? We have EU and UK patient data.
25:25 Speaker 1 - Evan: We support region pinning and data locality guarantees in Private deployments and Dedicated with region isolation; for hosted we'll document region residency controls. We'll add data residency language into the DPA addendum.

28:00 Speaker 4 - Priya: One small note, sometimes terminology gets fuzzy in transcripts — I might say KV cache but rendered as K V cash, but it's KV cache (key-value cache) that we manage for latency improvements.
28:12 Speaker 5 - Mark: Got it, sorry, I thought you said K V cash, that sounded like a money thing.

30:45 Speaker 2 - Jordan: Procurement also asked about subcontractor lists and whether Redwood will notify changes to subprocessors within 30 days.
30:58 Speaker 1 - Evan: We can commit to notifying significant subprocessor changes within 30 days, and provide an SLA for subprocessor onboarding.

33:10 Speaker 3 - Talia: For the pilot we want to confirm that model weights won't be stored outside our region and that model logs with patient data are redacted.
33:25 Speaker 4 - Priya: We'll enforce redaction rules on request and can route logs to your environment for redaction if needed. For model weights, standard hosted models are centrally stored, but Dedicated with private deployment keeps models in your tenant.

36:00 Speaker 5 - Mark: From engineering perspective we need a contact for networking preflight and a checklist for firewall rules and peering.
36:10 Speaker 1 - Evan: I'll include our networking checklist in the follow-up package and Priya will be the SE contact for the implementation.

39:05 Speaker 2 - Jordan: One more thing — billing cadence and invoicing. Do you support net-45?
39:14 Speaker 1 - Evan: Standard is net-30 but enterprise terms can be negotiated to net-45 on annual contracts. We'll push that in the commercial proposal.

41:30 Speaker 4 - Priya: Quick note on performance: we'll also provide an A/B evaluation harness for output quality so Aperture can run your prompt sets against our models and compare. That will be part of the benchmark artifacts.

44:02 Speaker 2 - Jordan: Great, so recap and next steps?
44:10 Speaker 1 - Evan: Recap: Evan to send MSA+DPA redlines and commercial pricing matrix; Priya to send benchmark spreadsheet and network checklist; Talia to send security questionnaire; Mark to provide token volume estimates. We'll aim to have the pilot scope doc within three business days.
44:27 Speaker 3 - Talia: Sounds good. We'll also start the procurement intake and try to align legal timelines.

48:00 Speaker 5 - Mark: Any competitors you think we should compare?
48:05 Speaker 1 - Evan: Some customers evaluate CloudAI or VertexAI; we can put together a brief comparison focused on latency, dedicated options, and cost.

50:10 Speaker 2 - Jordan: Okay thanks everyone, we'll look for the docs and follow up.
50:17 Speaker 1 - Evan: Thanks all, appreciate the time.
